name: Christian corporatism
summary: Christian corporatism holds that society is an organic body in which employers and workers of each industry or profession should cooperate in vocational groups, in place of class struggle, under a state that directs and supports rather than absorbs. It defends private property with a social duty, a family wage and wide ownership of small property, and rejects both liberal individualism and socialism, resting this third course on Christian morals and the Church.
scope: The Catholic corporatism of Rerum novarum (1891) and Quadragesimo anno (1931), the two texts the scholarship (Vieira de Sousa) names as the core of its teaching, with Heinrich Pesch's solidarism behind them. Answers rest on what those two encyclicals themselves state. Quadragesimo anno's description of Italy's syndicates (paragraphs 91-95) is a report with reservations, not the ideology's own programme. The Austrian Ständestaat, which scholarship links to the doctrine, is not used as the ideology's record: the sources read do not show its practice as part of what the ideology holds. It excludes Protestant corporatism, Mussolini's corporate state and postwar neo-corporatism.

notes: Evidence this pass is the full text of Rerum novarum and Quadragesimo anno (Vatican site) and Vieira de Sousa's 2007 scholarly article on Catholic corporatism. The earlier pass's answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries of the Austrian regime or on inference from the doctrine were nulled unless the encyclicals settle the statement; where an answer was kept or changed, its rationale cites paragraphs checked in the saved text. Themes searched in the encyclicals: property and inheritance, wages and the family wage, hours and child and women's labour, strikes and associations, the state's duties and subsidiarity, vocational groups, class, socialism and communism, religion and the Church in public life, charity and the poor, law and obedience, international economic cooperation (paragraph 89 only). The texts are silent on most social issues, criminal justice, immigration, environment, technology, foreign policy and many modern questions, so those are null. Quadragesimo anno 114 (certain kinds of property reserved to the State) and 85-87 (free vocational associations) were read against earlier answers on public ownership and state-recognised bargaining and both were nulled. The uncertainty rule is applied by the validator, not argued here.
